name: Storytime/Commentary
description: First-person narrative storytelling with dramatic pacing, reaction cuts, and emotional beats. Ideal for personal stories, life lessons, and candid experiences.
voice_style: intimate, conversational, emotionally present — like confiding in a close friend; dynamic range from quiet to emphatic
music_mood: cinematic underscore, emotional piano, ambient tension — music enters and exits with story beats

scene_sequence.narration_prompt: I almost got fired two weeks before my wedding. Here's what my boss said to me that I've never forgotten.
scene_sequence.visual_prompt: Person sitting still looking directly at camera, slightly dramatic lighting, ambient background out of focus, confident eye contact
scene_sequence.camera_movement: static medium close-up, hold on direct eye contact, slight slow push-in on 'I've never forgotten'
scene_sequence.lighting_setup: single dramatic key light slightly above and to the side, deep shadows on opposite side, background completely dark or softly blurred
scene_sequence.hailuo_style_note: Dark cinematic setup signals 'this story matters'; direct eye contact and slow push-in builds anticipation without rushing

scene_sequence.narration_prompt: It was 4pm on a Friday. I was packing up when my manager's Slack notification popped up. 'Can you stay back? Just 5 minutes.' Those five minutes lasted two hours.
scene_sequence.visual_prompt: Laptop screen with Slack notification, clock showing 4pm, person sitting down slowly, dark office with one overhead light on, chair creaking
scene_sequence.camera_movement: cut to screen insert, static hold on person sitting, slow zoom on clock, ambient office atmosphere shot
scene_sequence.lighting_setup: harsh single overhead office light creating dramatic shadows, cold blue screen glow, dark moody atmosphere
scene_sequence.hailuo_style_note: Screen insert + real-world atmosphere creates documentary realism; dark moody lighting mirrors emotional weight of the situation

scene_sequence.narration_prompt: She sat across from me and said: 'You're not failing at your job. You're failing at asking for help. And that's a skill — and skills can be learned.' I cried in the bathroom for ten minutes after.
scene_sequence.visual_prompt: Two-person conversation over desk (slightly off-center), close-up of person processing, moment of silence, tears welling up, face in hands
scene_sequence.camera_movement: two-shot framing, slow push-in to face close-up on tears welling, hold in darkness on face in hands beat
scene_sequence.lighting_setup: warm lamp on desk as sole light source for conversation, warm tones on face, shift to single backlight only during crying beat
scene_sequence.hailuo_style_note: Two-shot with warm desk lamp builds intimacy; tears beat deserves darkest/quietest lighting — let emotion breathe

scene_sequence.narration_prompt: I learned to ask for help that day. Not because I wanted to — but because I had to. It's still the hardest thing I do. Drop a comment — what's the lesson you learned the hard way?
scene_sequence.visual_prompt: Person looking at camera, softer expression, slight smile of reflection, comment section preview text overlaid, warm lighting returning
scene_sequence.camera_movement: slow return to same framing as intro shot, establishing visual bookend, warm direct address
scene_sequence.lighting_setup: warm soft lighting returning — same as intro but warmer, signaling emotional resolution
scene_sequence.hailuo_style_note: Return to intro framing is a powerful visual bookend; lighting warmth increase signals emotional resolution and growth
